name: Michael Schmidt-Ruthenbeck Bros.
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Rainer) of the family stake in retailer Metro AG, held via the Meridian Stiftung structure
profile: Michael Schmidt-Ruthenbeck (b. 1942) and his brother Rainer are sons of Wilhelm Schmidt-Ruthenbeck, who co-founded the German cash-and-carry wholesaler Metro in 1963/64. The family has held a large minority stake in Metro AG (about 16% around 2011), controlled through the Meridian Foundation vehicle, and is based in Duisburg. Listing is a combined entry for the brothers.
interesting_fact: The Schmidt-Ruthenbeck family holding was a key swing shareholder during Czech investor Daniel Kretinsky's 2019-2020 push for control of Metro AG.
deep_cut_fact: The Karl Schmidt family of Duisburg merchants founded Stiftung Mercator in 1996 and named it after the cartographer Gerhard Mercator, who lived in Duisburg for decades; it is now one of Germany's largest private foundations, with a climate-resilient-society programme.
notes: Very private family; no personal web/social presence found. No death reported, but no recent public appearance found either (born 1942). The only institutional route is the family's Stiftung Mercator (Essen), which is not a personal office. Forbes entry dates from 1997.

name: Paul Georges Despature
current_role: Chairman of Edify (Despature family investment company); former chairman of Somfy's management board (1983-2014)
profile: Paul-Georges Despature is the patriarch of the French Despature family, which controls Somfy, the Cluses-based maker of motors and automation for blinds, shutters and gates. He ran Somfy as chairman of its management board from 1983 until the end of 2014, then moved to head the family investment arm Edify. His son Jean Guillaume Despature now chairs Somfy, which the family took private in 2022-23.
interesting_fact: The Despature family, which already owned the thermal-underwear brand Damart, bought Somfy in 1984 as a diversification into summer-season products; Somfy has since become a world leader in motorised blinds and the connected home.
deep_cut_fact: The name SOMFY is an acronym for 'Société d'Outillage et Mécanique du FaucignY', a 1969 spin-off of the Cluses precision-machining firm Carpano & Pons in the Arve valley, a region known for Swiss-watch part-making.

name: Leonard Schleifer
current_role: Co-founder, Board Co-Chair, President and CEO, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: REGN)
profile: Leonard Schleifer was a young neurologist and assistant professor at Cornell when he founded Regeneron in 1988, recruiting George Yancopoulos as co-founder. He took it public in 1991 and still runs the Tarrytown, NY company, which has 12 FDA-approved medicines, including the blockbuster eye drug Eylea and Dupixent (with Sanofi). He owns about 2% of the stock.
interesting_fact: The company name means 'regenerating neurons', with 'gene' hidden in the middle; the idea was first sketched on a napkin.
deep_cut_fact: At the urging of his Queens high-school math teacher, Schleifer entered the 1970 Westinghouse Science Talent Search, the competition Regeneron itself now sponsors as the Regeneron Science Talent Search.
notes: Active public figure who speaks regularly on drug pricing and science-led management. The best route is Regeneron corporate communications. Press and IR names come from 2026 earnings releases; check the latest release for current contacts.

name: Lucio Tan
current_role: Founder and Chairman, LT Group Inc. (tobacco, spirits, beer, banking, property; parent links to Philippine Airlines)
profile: Born in China and raised in the Philippines, Lucio Tan co-founded Fortune Tobacco in 1966 and built it into LT Group, with interests in tobacco (PMFTC), Tanduay rum, Asia Brewery (1982), Philippine National Bank and property. He also controls flag carrier Philippine Airlines through PAL Holdings. In 2023 his grandson Lucio Tan III became president of LT Group and PAL Holdings.
interesting_fact: Before becoming a tycoon he worked as a janitor in a tobacco factory while studying chemical engineering at Far Eastern University, and was later promoted to tobacco 'cook' mixing blends.
deep_cut_fact: Tan says he went to school barefoot as a child; decades later he was expanding into nickel mining to ride the EV-battery-driven nickel boom.
notes: In his 90s (born 1933/34); day-to-day leadership is moving to grandson Lucio Tan III. Enjoys riding helicopters (Forbes). LT Group IR is named in PSE Edge disclosures (https://edge.pse.com.ph/downloadHtml.do?file_id=1987230), but no clean email was verified. Very limited personal media presence.

name: Eddie Zakay
current_role: Deputy Chairman, Topland Group (London); brother Sol Zakay is Founder & CEO
profile: Eddie Zakay and his brother Sol built Topland Group, a privately owned London property and investment group, starting in the UK in the 1980s/90s. Topland made its name with counter-cyclical bets and large sale-and-leaseback deals with Marks & Spencer, Tesco and Eroski, and sold its 26 Hallmark hotels in 2019. Today it runs a multi-billion-pound portfolio, a bridging-loan arm and a roughly GBP 0.8bn development pipeline.
interesting_fact: Between 2000 and 2010 Topland completed more than GBP 1.5 billion of sale-and-leasebacks with retailers including Marks & Spencer, Tesco, Sainsbury's, Aldi and Eroski.
deep_cut_fact: In the 2010s Topland moved beyond property into renewable-energy investing, and was an early aggregator of UK supported-living housing before selling the portfolio to long-term holders including Civitas.

name: Pritviraj Jindal
current_role: Chairperson (Non-Executive), Jindal SAW Ltd. (O.P. Jindal Group)
profile: Prithavi Raj (P.R.) Jindal is the eldest son of O.P. Jindal, founder of the O.P. Jindal Group. When the group was split among the four brothers, he took Jindal SAW, a leading maker of submerged-arc-welded line pipe for oil, gas and water, and the family cross-holdings give him stakes in JSW Steel and other group companies. His daughters Sminu Jindal (MD) and Shraddha (Joint MD) now help run Jindal SAW.
interesting_fact: Jindal SAW credits him with introducing SAW (submerged-arc-welded) pipe manufacturing in India more than four decades ago, helping make India one of the world's leading line-pipe makers.
deep_cut_fact: Besides steel pipes, he is listed as a director of Sonabheel Tea Limited, a tea company, among his other board seats.
notes: Company spells his name 'Prithavi Raj Jindal' (also P.R. Jindal). Listed under UAE by Hurun. Low personal media profile; route through Jindal SAW corporate office (New Delhi). Pipe and energy-infrastructure angle (oil and gas, water) fits the podcast.

name: Jonathan Tisch
current_role: Executive Chairman, Loews Hotels; co-owner, board member and treasurer of the New York Giants; chairman of The Shed (NYC)
profile: Jonathan Tisch is the son of Bob Tisch, who co-founded Loews Corporation with his brother Laurence in 1946. Jonathan has led Loews Hotels since 1989 and was co-chairman of Loews Corp. until stepping back from its board at the end of 2024; he is now Executive Chairman of Loews Hotels. The family also owns 50% of the New York Giants, and he is a prominent civic philanthropist and chairman emeritus of the U.S. Travel Association.
interesting_fact: He hosts the interview programme 'Beyond the Boardroom with Jonathan Tisch' and has co-written three books, including 'Chocolates on the Pillow Aren't Enough: Reinventing the Customer Experience' (2007).
deep_cut_fact: In 1990, a year after becoming chairman of Loews Hotels, he launched the Loews Hotels 'Good Neighbor Policy' committing hotels to local community engagement. His $40M gift created the Tisch College of Civic Life at Tufts, his alma mater (class of 1976).
notes: Very media-friendly: a host and author himself, so a strong podcast candidate. Loews also owns natural-gas pipelines (Boardwalk), an energy angle. SEC data still lists him as a Loews director, but Wikipedia says he left the Loews Corp board on 31 Dec 2024; check before outreach.

name: Hong Hao
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Asymchem Laboratories (凯莱英医药集团), Tianjin; listed in Shenzhen (2016) and Hong Kong (2021)
profile: Dr. Hao Hong (洪浩) holds a PhD in medicinal chemistry from the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and founded Asymchem in 1995. He built it into a leading CDMO making active ingredients for innovative drugs for global pharma, with more than 10,000 staff and R&D and manufacturing sites in China, the US and the UK. The company positions itself as a leader in green pharmaceutical technology.
interesting_fact: Asymchem, now a Tianjin-headquartered Chinese pharma-outsourcing leader, was founded in 1995 in North Carolina, USA.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Asymchem he was a postdoctoral researcher in medicinal chemistry at the University of Georgia, and he has published dozens of papers in the Journal of Organic Chemistry (JOC) and JACS.
notes: Input 'Casymchen' = Asymchem (凯莱英). He goes by 'Dr. Hao Hong' in English. The company also publishes securities@asymchem.com.cn for securities affairs. A scientist-entrepreneur, which may suit the entrepreneurship theme.

name: Zhuo Jun
current_role: Director and major shareholder, Shenzhen Kinwong Electronic Co. (Shanghai-listed PCB maker)
profile: Zhuo Jun inherited a large stake in Shenzhen Kinwong Electronic after her husband and co-founder Shen Jitang died in 2013. Kinwong, founded in Shenzhen's Nanshan District in 1993, is one of China's largest printed-circuit-board makers. She sits on its board, and her younger brother Zhuo Yong is vice chairman. The company announced a Hong Kong dual listing in 2025.
interesting_fact: Kinwong is building its first overseas manufacturing base, a PCB plant in Thailand, due to start production in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: After high school she spent four years as a clerk at the Heung Yee Kuk, the statutory advisory body representing the interests of Hong Kong's New Territories.
notes: Very low public profile and not an executive spokesperson; the company route goes via the IR/securities office. PCBs for servers and data-centre hardware are relevant to the podcast. The deep-cut fact comes from Forbes, which already appeared in the input.

It grew into India's fourth-largest drugmaker by domestic sales, selling affordable generics and consumer brands, and listed on NSE/BSE in May 2023. Arora oversees finance, HR and operations.

name: Edward Lampert
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, ESL Investments; Chairman, Transform Holdco (Transformco, owner of the former Sears Holdings assets)
profile: Eddie Lampert interned at Goldman Sachs and worked in its risk-arbitrage department before founding the Greenwich, CT hedge fund ESL Investments in 1988 at age 25. He merged Kmart and Sears in 2005 and was Sears Holdings' CEO from 2013. After its 2018 bankruptcy his Transformco bought the assets, and he also holds 10%+ stakes in Lands' End and Seritage.
interesting_fact: Time named him to its 2006 Time 100 list, and a 2004 Businessweek profile compared his investing style to Warren Buffett's.
deep_cut_fact: His interest in investing was sparked by his grandmother, a passive investor. At Goldman (1985-88) he worked directly with Robert Rubin in risk arbitrage. As a teenager after his father's death he stocked shelves and filled orders in warehouses after school.
notes: Media-shy; rarely gives interviews, and the Sears story is a sensitive topic. The ESL and Transformco sites were unreachable from here, so no verified press contact was captured. Skull and Bones (Yale '84). Avoid the 2003 kidnapping in outreach.
